label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**Subject: Tuesday reading club at Knocknacarra, new numbers, and a confession**

Dear Niamh,

Thanks for your email of the 30th about pausing the Tuesday club after Christmas. I understand the reasons, and I know the hall insurance going up isn't something you can wave away. But the picture has changed a good deal in the past few weeks, and I wanted you to have the new numbers in front of you before the review meeting on the 18th.

When we started, we had five children most weeks in September, and I'll admit I had my doubts myself. By mid-October we were up to nine. On Tuesday the 3rd we had fourteen children in the meeting room upstairs, and we were running short of chairs.

Some of that is down to Declan Moran at the Salthill Book Nook, who very kindly donated 120 books. Most of them suit the 6 to 9 age group, which is exactly where we needed them, and a good few are as Gaeilge. Having that many new books on the table has made a real difference. The children come in and go straight to them.

The numbers don't tell the whole story, though. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and at the end of every session now the older girl reads to the younger one in English. It's lovely to watch. There's also a boy who wouldn't so much as open a book in September, and last week he asked me could he take two home. Thirty-odd years in a classroom and that still gets me.

I'd be very sorry to see it paused just as it has taken off. I'd ask you to look at these figures again before the 18th and reconsider. If there's anything else you'd find useful for the meeting, a list of the sessions or a word from some of the parents, I'm happy to pull it together.

Now, the confession. I was at the farmers' market and got talking to Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier. I was so full of all this that I told her the whole story and said "come along any Tuesday." She has since been in touch and would like to come on Tuesday the 24th with a photographer.

I know perfectly well that photographs of the children need your sign-off and the parental consent forms first, and I should have checked with you before saying a word to her. I was wrong not to, plain and simple. I'd rather you heard it from me than from anyone else.

Here's what I'd suggest. I'll ring Orla this week and tell her the visit is on hold until you've had a chance to decide. If you're happy for it to go ahead, I'll gladly collect the consent forms from the parents myself, so it's no extra work on your end. If you'd prefer it didn't happen at all, or not just yet, that's your call and I'll let her know.

I do think some coverage could do the club a lot of good, and maybe help make the case for keeping it going, but only if it's done properly and through you.

Thanks, Niamh, for everything you do keeping all of us organised. Do let me know what you think, and I'll talk to you before the 18th if not before.

Warm regards,
[Your name]

---

One thing to check: you mentioned the 3rd as "last Tuesday," but going by today's date (the 11th), the most recent Tuesday was the 10th. I wrote "Tuesday the 3rd" so the email is accurate either way. If you had a session on the 10th, it would be worth adding that week's numbers too.
